observation_text: Child was asked to put away toys after playtime.
behavior: Child started to cry and refused to put toys away.
consequence: Child eventually helped put away toys after being offered a sticker.
caregiver_response: Used distraction to encourage participation.
suggested_followup_question: What types of activities do you think would help ease transitions?
general_support_idea: Offering choices during transitions can encourage cooperation.

observation_text: Child was told it was time to leave the playground.
behavior: Child yelled that they didn't want to leave and ran away from the caregiver.
consequence: Child eventually returned when their friend called them over.
caregiver_response: Gave space before calling the child back.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make transitions from playtime smoother?
general_support_idea: Creating a countdown to transitions may help prepare the child.

observation_text: Child was asked to get ready for dinner after playing.
behavior: Child threw a toy and shouted in frustration.
consequence: Child calmed down after being shown a favorite dinner was ready.
caregiver_response: Offered a favorite food to ease the transition.
suggested_followup_question: What other strategies can help during mealtimes?
general_support_idea: Involving the child in setting the table can aid transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to stop playing video games and get ready for bed.
behavior: Child argued and refused to turn off the game.
consequence: Child turned off the game after a 5-minute warning was given.
caregiver_response: Set a timer to signal the end of playtime.
suggested_followup_question: How can we create a better bedtime routine?
general_support_idea: Discussing the next day's plans can make bedtime smoother.

observation_text: Child was told it was time to leave the store.
behavior: Child dropped to the floor and refused to move.
consequence: Child eventually stood up and followed the caregiver after being offered a toy to hold.
emotion_context: Frustrated by the abrupt ending of the outing.
caregiver_response: Found a distraction to help the child move along.
suggested_followup_question: What are some favorite items to bring when shopping?
general_support_idea: Bringing a small toy can help during outings.

observation_text: Child was told it was time to switch from art to snack time.
behavior: Child picked up their art supplies and started to cry.
consequence: Child calmed down after being offered a choice between snacks.
caregiver_response: Gave a couple of options for snack choices.
suggested_followup_question: What snacks do they enjoy most?
general_support_idea: Involving children in snack prep can ease transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to pack up their things after playtime.
antecedent: Transition to next activity was announced.
behavior: Child started talking back and refused to listen to instructions.
consequence: Child complied after being reminded of the next fun activity planned.
caregiver_response: Used positive reinforcement to encourage packing.
suggested_followup_question: What activities can help maintain attention during transitions?
general_support_idea: Incorporating fun songs for packing can be effective.

observation_text: Child was told to leave the playground for a family gathering.
antecedent: Family was waiting in the car.
behavior: Child walked slowly and kept looking back at the playground.
consequence: Child arrived at the car and engaged in conversation about their day.
caregiver_response: Engaged child in conversation to keep them moving.
suggested_followup_question: How can we manage social time better?
general_support_idea: Discuss plans for future playdates to ease transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to switch from playing outside to homework time.
behavior: Child complained and said they were not ready to stop playing.
consequence: Child began homework after a reminder about a favorite activity they could do after.
caregiver_response: Promised a break after homework was finished.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to help with homework motivation?
general_support_idea: Setting a timer for breaks can help manage transitions.

observation_text: Child was told it was time to leave a friend's house.
behavior: Child argued and started to pack toys into a bag to take home.
consequence: Child eventually left with the toys after being reminded it was getting late.
caregiver_response: Acknowledged the attachment to toys during the transition.
suggested_followup_question: What toy made the most impact on them today?
general_support_idea: Offering a special item for the ride home can help.

observation_text: Child was supposed to transition from school to an after-school program.
behavior: Child attempted to leave the school grounds.
consequence: Child returned after being called back by the caregiver.
possible_trigger: Child started running towards the street, ignoring calls.
caregiver_response: Actively reminded child of the supervision in the program.
suggested_followup_question: How can we ensure the child feels safer during transitions?
general_support_idea: Discussing the after-school program in advance might help.

observation_text: Child was asked to stop playing video games to leave for a family event.
behavior: Child started yelling and knocked over a chair.
consequence: Child calmed down after a moment and helped clean up the chair.
emotion_context: Frustrated by the abrupt end of fun.
caregiver_response: Helped clean up and talked about the event afterward.
suggested_followup_question: How can we prepare them for the event?
general_support_idea: Creating a visual schedule for the day might help.

observation_text: Child was asked to stop playing outside and come inside for dinner.
behavior: Child sat on the ground and refused to get up.
consequence: Child eventually stood up and walked inside after a favorite food was mentioned.
emotion_context: Frustrated by the transition from outside to inside.
caregiver_response: Used favorite food as motivation.
suggested_followup_question: What other strategies can help with dinner time?
general_support_idea: Offering a fun dinner theme might engage them.

observation_text: Child was told it was time for bed.
behavior: Child ran around and refused to get ready for bed.
consequence: Child followed the caregiver to the bathroom after being offered a bedtime story.
caregiver_response: Told a story while getting ready to ease tension.
suggested_followup_question: What calming routines can we establish for bedtime?
general_support_idea: Reading together at bedtime can improve transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to transition from play to homework.
behavior: Child argued and refused to stop playing video games.
consequence: Child put the game away after being reminded of an upcoming deadline.
caregiver_response: Offered to help organize the homework.
suggested_followup_question: What tools might help them focus better?
general_support_idea: Setting specific times to work can help with focus.

observation_text: Child was asked to leave a family gathering.
antecedent: Time to go home was announced.
behavior: Child threw a tantrum and refused to move.
consequence: Child calmed down after seeing a favorite toy in the car.
caregiver_response: Used distraction to keep things moving along.

general_support_idea: Talking about future gatherings can help ease transition anxiety.

observation_text: Child was asked to stop playing a game to go home.
behavior: Child got up and walked away in silence.
consequence: Child eventually joined the caregiver after being reassured they could play next time.
caregiver_response: Gave a heads-up before leaving.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help them feel involved in travel plans?
general_support_idea: Discussing travel plans can ease the transition.

observation_text: Child was told it was time to leave the playground.
behavior: Child started to wander away and looked towards the swings.
consequence: Child returned to the caregiver after being reminded of the time.
caregiver_response: Gave a gentle reminder of the time.
suggested_followup_question: What other strategies could help with transitions?
general_support_idea: Using visual cues about time can aid understanding.

observation_text: Child was asked to stop playing and prepare for bed.
behavior: Child started throwing their toys around.
consequence: Child calmed down and helped tidy up the toys after a short talk.
caregiver_response: Talked about the need for sleep and next day's activities.
suggested_followup_question: How to encourage cooperation during bedtime?
general_support_idea: Creating a bedtime checklist could help ease transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to transition from playtime to snack time. They suddenly shouted, 'No! I want to keep playing!'
behavior: Child shouted and sat on the floor with arms crossed.
consequence: Child eventually got up after a few minutes and went to the table.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a countdown for the transition.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make transitions easier for them?
general_support_idea: Offering a visual timer for upcoming transitions may help.

observation_text: While leaving the school playground, the child hesitated and looked back at their friends, saying, 'I don’t want to go yet.'
behavior: Child stood still and refused to walk towards the exit.
consequence: Child eventually walked out when a friend waved goodbye.
caregiver_response: Caregiver encouraged them to say goodbye and join them.
suggested_followup_question: What helps your child part from friends?
general_support_idea: Discussing the fun planned for later may ease transitions.

observation_text: After finishing a game at daycare, the child was asked to help clean up but began to play with the toys instead.
behavior: Child ignored the request and played with the toys.
consequence: Child helped after the caregiver started singing a cleanup song.
caregiver_response: Caregiver joined in the cleanup song to engage them.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies work for cleanup time?
general_support_idea: Incorporating music during transitions can be effective.

observation_text: During a family outing at a restaurant, the child spotted a toy display and ran towards it, leaving the caregiver behind.
behavior: Child ran away towards the toys, ignoring the caregiver’s call to stay close.
consequence: Child was redirected and returned after the caregiver caught up.
caregiver_response: Caregiver calmly explained the importance of staying together.
suggested_followup_question: How can we keep them close in busy places?
general_support_idea: Establishing a meeting point while out can help.
